A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HippoRAG 2 study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and Appendices A-G support comparison, including material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original QA and retrieval experiments, component ablations, sensitivity tests, error analysis, and indexing-cost measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds corpus-expansion experiments, statistical significance findings, and runtime and memory measurements.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the same OpenIE graph construction, passage-node integration, query-to-triple matching, recognition filtering, and Personalized PageRank retrieval with dense-retrieval fallback. Section 3.1 expands the explanation without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: The seven benchmark datasets and three task categories remain unchanged. v2 adds a growing-corpus test scenario on NQ and MuSiQue, extending evaluation to incremental changes in the retrieval environment.

E2.justification: The QA and retrieval comparator sets are unchanged. Appendix F and Table 12 add NV-Embed-v2 and HippoRAG to the resource comparison, which previously compared HippoRAG 2 with RAPTOR, LightRAG, and GraphRAG.

E3.justification: Section 6.3 introduces four corpus segments, evaluating approximately 250 fixed questions while adding the remaining segments. Appendix F adds indexing-time, query-time, and GPU-memory metrics, excluding model weights. Table 14 also swaps GraphRAG/LightRAG headings, reassigning model-specific settings such as the 2,000-token community-report limit; this changes the reported protocol without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused corpus-expansion robustness analysis in Section 6.3/Figure 3 and broadens Appendix F's efficiency analysis beyond token usage. Existing component ablations, reset-weight sensitivity, retriever-flexibility tests, qualitative examples, and error analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Table 2 newly reports bootstrap significance testing of HippoRAG 2 against NV-Embed-v2 at p < 0.05. v1 provides no corresponding test. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts or confidence intervals, and v2 does not specify the bootstrap resample count.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation scores remain unchanged. v2 adds corpus-growth F1 curves, significant QA comparisons on NQ, MuSiQue, 2Wiki, and LV-Eval, and resource results such as HippoRAG 2's 99.5-minute indexing, 1.2-second query time, and 9.9-GB memory usage excluding weights. v1's 1.1-second-per-passage estimate and GPT-4o-mini indexing estimates of under $2 and within 24 hours are removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical content is unchanged, including the filtered-triple subset relation and PPR scoring description. Expanded explanations of seed nodes and reset probabilities introduce no new formal definitions, derivations, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about factual, sense-making, and associative memory, including the stated seven-point associative-task improvement. The additional experiments support the existing framing rather than redefine it.

C2.justification: Section 6.3 newly argues that different degradation patterns on simple and multi-hop QA motivate varied task complexities in continual-learning benchmarks. Appendix F adds an explicit accuracy-versus-resource tradeoff, acknowledging increased memory from fact embeddings and lower efficiency than standard RAG.

D1.justification: The abstract changes code/data status from a future release to reported availability. Section 4.4 explicitly documents using five retrieved passages for QA, and Appendix F documents the memory-accounting convention. Conversely, v2 removes the exact gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 identifier and batch-API deployment details; Table 14 revises baseline-specific hyperparameter attribution.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds references to StreamingQA, Carpe diem, Tic-LM, and Roth et al.'s continual multimodal pretraining work. The core positioning relative to existing RAG methods remains unchanged. GritLM and NV-Embed publication updates concern the same cited works.

P1.justification: v2 locally expands the HippoRAG overview and baseline descriptions, reformats the task categories, adds Section 6.3, and rewrites Appendix F. Most of the narrative and the overall section and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the corpus-expansion plot, expands Table 12 with additional methods and resource rows, and adds significance markers to Table 2. Dataset and analysis tables are relocated, Tables 6/7 exchange numbering, and appendix figures are renumbered; the existing method, prompt, and pipeline diagrams remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The limited corpus-growth experiment gives more direct support to the continual-learning framing, while bootstrap reporting and runtime/memory comparisons make the evidence easier to assess. Clearer explanations and reported code/data availability also help. These benefits outweigh the removed GPT-4o-mini deployment details and minor new reporting inconsistencies, such as Table 12 labeling the 13.3/1.2-second ratio as 1008.3%. The method and core accuracy results remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
